record.paper_title: Regularity of maximal operators: recent progress and some open problems
record.original_question: For radial functions f in W^{1,1}(R^d), Luiro proved that the uncentered Hardy-Littlewood maximal function is weakly differentiable and satisfies ||grad M_tilde f||_{L^1(R^d)} <= C(d)||grad f||_{L^1(R^d)}. Does the same endpoint W^{1,1} to L^1 gradient bound hold for the centered Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator M acting on radial functions?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $d \ge 2$. For a locally integrable function $f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}$, define the centered Hardy–Littlewood maximal function
$$ Mf(x) \;=\; \sup_{r>0} \frac{1}{|B(x,r)|}\int_{B(x,r)} |f(y)|\,dy, $$
where $B(x,r)$ denotes the open Euclidean ball of radius $r$ centered at $x$.

Call $f$ radial if $f(x)=f(|x|)$ for almost every $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$. Let $W^{1,1}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ denote the Sobolev space of $L^1$ functions with weak gradient in $L^1(\mathbb{R}^d)$.

It is known (Luiro) that the uncentered Hardy–Littlewood maximal operator $\widetilde{M}$, defined by
$$ \widetilde{M}f(x) \;=\; \sup_{B\ni x} \frac{1}{|B|}\int_{B}|f(y)|\,dy $$
(supremum over all balls $B$ containing $x$), satisfies, for every radial $f\in W^{1,1}(\mathbb{R}^d)$, that $\widetilde{M}f$ is weakly differentiable and
$$ \|\nabla \widetilde{M}f\|_{L^1(\mathbb{R}^d)} \;\le\; C(d)\,\|\nabla f\|_{L^1(\mathbb{R}^d)} $$
for some constant $C(d)$ depending only on $d$.

Prove or disprove the analogous endpoint statement for the centered maximal operator: for every radial $f\in W^{1,1}(\mathbb{R}^d)$, the function $Mf$ is weakly differentiable and there exists a constant $C(d)$ such that
$$ \|\nabla M f\|_{L^1(\mathbb{R}^d)} \;\le\; C(d)\,\|\nabla f\|_{L^1(\mathbb{R}^d)}. $$
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work has established the analogous radial endpoint gradient bound for smooth-kernel centered maximal operators (heat-flow and Poisson maximal functions) but explicitly leaves the centered Hardy–Littlewood maximal operator case unresolved. No publication appears to settle the centered HL radial endpoint $W^{1,1}\to L^1$ gradient bound in dimensions $d\ge 2$, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Gradient bounds for radial maximal functions (arXiv:1906.01487)
status_evidence.snippet: For the heat flow maximal operator and the Poisson maximal operator, the analogue of Luiro's result is established in a centered setting with smooth kernels.
status_evidence.claim: The centered analogue is proved only for smooth-kernel (heat/Poisson) maximal operators, not for the centered Hardy–Littlewood maximal operator itself.

status_evidence.title: Endpoint Sobolev Bounds for Fractional Hardy-Littlewood Maximal Operators (arXiv:2010.05561)
status_evidence.snippet: Endpoint gradient bounds for the fractional centered/uncentered HL maximal operators for 0<α<1.
status_evidence.claim: Endpoint Sobolev results have advanced in the fractional regime, but the non-fractional centered HL radial endpoint bound is still discussed as an outstanding question.
